ledger.claim: The governing distance figure is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace measures 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass and a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 283 fixes on a 10-second sampling interval, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds. No limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, so the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone and no independent corroboration is needed for that finding.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. All three core artifacts carry the same trip identifier TRP-00104, and the trace begins at the recorded pickup event (first fix 20:35:10, started_at 20:35:10), so the artifacts describe the same trip; and the excess of 7.07 km clears both POL-RD-01 thresholds on an unimpaired trace.

The one valid excuse the driver has is the LTA accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link — the optimal route is PIE westbound throughout, the advisory window (20:02–21:35) straddles the trip, and the trace leaves the PIE before the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE. POL-RD-03 therefore applies, but only within its own cap: the justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.9) = 4.9 km. The clause exonerates 4.9 km, not the 7.07 km actually driven.

The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 27.1 + 4.9 = 32.0 km, with a duration of 34.0 x (32.0 / 27.1) = 40.1 minutes. The driver's trace is 34.17 km, which is itself longer than the 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative he was entitled to use, and the 2.17 km of excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and falls to be refunded under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted route. The rider's own chat reply, 'not too long ah', shows the detour he consented to was a modest one, not a run down to Marina and along the AYE.

The second advisory the driver relies on, ADV-20260716-055 for a CTE breakdown, exonerates nothing. It is impaired at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, and I disclose that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Its geometry (lat 1.365–1.39) covers a corridor this trip never enters, so it cannot satisfy POL-RD-03, which provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses does not exonerate anything.

POL-RD-04 does not rescue the remainder. The chat log shows the driver proposing the diversion ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider merely acknowledging it. That message names no place or road, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the rider-instruction exoneration cannot be made out and the excess stands.

The fare model is METERED: fare_model is 'METERED' and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. The rider paid the meter on 34.2 charged km driven at 47 charged minutes, and is entitled to be recomputed to the adjusted optimal.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the closure-adjusted route is: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 32.0 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828, with no ERP, tolls, surcharge, waiting fee or promo to add. Charged total is 43.41, so the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing here, and I do not press it beyond its terms: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge and no off-route or phantom line, and the trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction to sit alongside the distance refund.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires on this record: the identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or out-of-window artifact, the refund is far below SGD 150, and every charge line has a counterpart. The tribunal should rule on the money rather than escalate.

The platform's own optimal route for this trip runs the PIE westbound and nothing else, and the LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) is a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident with 2 of 3 lanes blocked on the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — precisely a road and expressway segment the optimal route traverses. The advisory is active 20:02-21:35 and overlaps the trip window of 20:35-21:22 by 53.1 minutes, so the 15-minute buffer at each end required by limb (b) is comfortably met. The advisory artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no discount attaches to it. Limbs (a) and (b) of POL-RD-03 are satisfied.

Limb (c) of POL-RD-03 is satisfied on the telemetry: the unimpaired 283-fix trace in EV-GPS-00104 shows the vehicle leaving the optimal PIE corridor at the Bedok North Ave 4 exit ahead of the blocked segment and rejoining it on the AYE after the accident — the 'leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after' pattern the clause requires, rather than a crossing of the closed stretch. The admissibility note on EV-GPS-00104 records exactly this exit-and-rejoin geometry over 100% coverage.

Exoneration under POL-RD-03 is capped, and the cap still excuses the bulk of the alleged excess. The measured excess is 7.07 km; the cap is 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00 = 4.90 km, so the justified excess is min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km and only 2.17 km of the rider's 7.07 km figure remains uncured. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is therefore 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.0 km, and its duration scaled from the booked 34.0 minutes is 34.0 x (32.0 / 27.1) = 40.1 minutes; amended_optimal_duration_min is null, so the scaled figure governs.

Run the POL-RD-02 arithmetic against the closure-adjusted optimal, not the booked one: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 32.0 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.83, against a charged total of 43.41, and the refund is 3.58 rounded UP to SGD 3.60. That is the limit of what the rider can recover — roughly a quarter of the SGD 14.00 claimed. The fare model is METERED with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, so POL-RD-11 does not run and there is no upfront-quote route to a larger award.

The driver discharges the burden that shifts to him under POL-RD-08: he points to a specific artifact and a specific clause — EV-ADVIS-00104-01, the LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007, and POL-RD-03 — rather than a general assertion that traffic was bad. The advisory carries a real advisory ID, the named road matches the optimal corridor, and shortest_lawful_alternative_km of 30.1 km is recorded on it, which is what makes the POL-RD-03 cap computable at all.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists and POL-RD-06 should not be pressed against this driver. This trip is not a MATERIAL deviation in the first place — 7.07 km is under the 8.0 km limb and 26.09% is under the 50% limb of POL-RD-01 — and on the clause's own counters driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a rate of 0.0035, far below the 0.05 threshold, with 1 far below the threshold of 3. No FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available on this profile.

The telemetry is clean and none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs fires: EV-GPS-00104 carries 283 fixes at an expected and actual sample interval of 10 seconds, 100% coverage, a gaps array that is empty and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. There is no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so the deviation is measured on an unimpaired trace and no independent-corroboration requirement arises.

The chat log corroborates the driver's account in real time, which is why the diversion cannot be characterised as an unexplained detour: at 20:38:12, minutes after the trip started at 20:35:10, the driver told the rider 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok', and the rider replied 'ok but not too long ah' at 20:38:55. The driver announced the PIE accident contemporaneously with the event the LTA advisory records, and the rider raised no objection at the time.

Nothing may be added on top under the pass-through clause: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries, no tolls, a zero airport surcharge (and this trip does not originate at an airport) and no waiting-time fee, so nothing is refundable under POL-RD-09's limbs (1) to (4). Nor does POL-RD-04's compensation limb arise — the distance charged of 34.2 km does not fall short of the 34.17 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall for the driver to claim. The only money in issue is the distance-and-time excess.

The driver does not rest any part of his case on the second advisory, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, and that artifact is disclosed as impaired: its weight_multiplier is 0.25 and it carries the issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, with its geometry describing a CTE corridor this trip never enters. Because the deciding fact here — the closure on the optimal corridor — is carried by weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-ADVIS-00104-01 and EV-GPS-00104), the impaired advisory does not cap the confidence of any finding built on it under POL-GEN-02, and it should be left out of account altogether.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a real route deviation, but only part of the extra distance is refundable to the rider and the rest is justified by a genuine road closure.

What is established. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104) is the governing distance measurement: 34.17 km driven against a booked optimal of 27.1 km (EV-TRIP-00104) — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 tests (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I have used the trace figure, not the rounded 34.2 km convenience copy on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 283 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10-second interval, an empty gaps array and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) fires and no independent corroboration was required.

The driver's PIE closure. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0) names a HIGH-severity accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link — the very road the booked optimal route uses — and its 20:02–21:35 window straddles the whole trip. The trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked stretch and rejoins afterwards, so POL-RD-03 applies. But it applies only up to its cap: min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. That 4.90 km is exonerated; the remaining 2.17 km is not.

The second advisory, ADV-20260716-055 (EV-ADVIS-00104-02), is impaired: weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, and its geometry describes a CTE corridor this trip never enters. It exonerates nothing. Because the finding does not rest on it, that discount does not cap the confidence of this ruling, but the artifact is named here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires.

The rider's chat reply. EV-CHAT-00104 shows the driver proposing 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok' at 20:38:12 and the rider answering 'ok but not too long ah' at 20:38:55. That does not make the detour rider-requested under POL-RD-04: the instruction came from the driver, the rider named no road or place, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the clause's corroboration test could not be run and the clause is unavailable. The rider's acknowledgement does not transfer the uncured excess to him.

The refund. EV-FARE-00104 shows fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not run and POL-RD-02 governs. Against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.0 km and 40.1 minutes:
  recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 32.0 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828
  charged_total = 43.41
  refund = 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60
There is no ERP, toll, airport surcharge (the trip does not originate at an airport), waiting fee or promo line to add, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing, and POL-RD-04's compensation limb does not arise because the distance charged (34.2 km) does not fall short of the trace by more than 1.0 km.

No repeat pattern. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km materiality limb and 26.09% is far below 50%, and on the driver's profile deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 completed trips in 90 days — no pattern, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; every exculpatory clause invoked was matched to a present, in-window artifact; and the refund is far below SGD 150. Both parties' remaining claims (rider POL-RD-08 burden, POL-RD-07 integrity, and the unused POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-04 limbs) are consistent with this analysis and do not move the figure.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.60 to the rider. The full SGD 14.00 claimed is not recoverable because the driver's diversion was substantially justified by a real, in-window PIE closure, and the capped exoneration leaves only 2.17 km of unjustified excess.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
